R09.label: REAL DATA EXTRACTS WITH TRANSCRIBED REPORT TABLES
R09.construction: Parts A-C quote and transcribe the ESO technical report (sections 6.2-6.4 and 7, Tables 8 and 9), Appendix M of its appendices, the E3C interim and final reports and Ofgem paragraph 3.23, every quotation and table cell checked on the stated PDF page (personal names in Table 8 replaced by roles). Part D indexes every held revision of the REMIT messages of T_HOWAO-1/2/3 and T_LBAR-1 (real Elexon data, unchanged; all fields in the CSV and the asset-log rows). Part E gives, for organisational posts and web statements, the decoded or displayed time and a gist written for this record (no gist shares more than three consecutive words with its source; not openly licensed). Part F quotes Ofgem and GOV.UK publications of 12-20 August 2019 (Open Government Licence). Ofgem's January 2020 enforcement settlements are excluded.

Part A heading
A1 ESO technical report section 6.2

sources.section: 6.2 Engagement with government and the regulator
sources.quote: The first communication between the ESO control room and BEIS was at 17:41hrs.

sources.section: 6.2 Engagement with government and the regulator
sources.quote: At this point the event was generally understood, demand restoration was in progress and further disturbances were considered unlikely.

sources.section: 6.2 Engagement with government and the regulator
sources.quote: The first communication with Ofgem was made at 17:51hrs with further communication at 18:17hrs and 18:45hrs and then throughout the weekend.

sources.section: 6.2 Engagement with government and the regulator
sources.quote: Further updates to BEIS from the ESO control room were made at 18:09hrs, 19:29hrs and 19:38hrs respectively.

segments.content: A2 ESO technical report section 7 (communications finding)

sources.quote: The ESO contacted BEIS at 17:40 and Ofgem at 18:00.
The initial media statement by the ESO issued at 18:27 with a subsequent statement at 20:06 and a video from the Head of National Control being posted at 20:11.

segments.content: A3 ESO appendices, Appendix M answers to E3C questions (Q34)

sources.section: Appendix M – ESO E3C Questions and Answers
sources.quote: These answers are all based on the data available to the ESO on 28 August 2019.
There appeared to be delays in escalations to Ofgem & BEIS after LFDD was initiated? Are there any lessons to be learnt?
At 17:10hrs, the ENCC Power System Manager (PSM) reported the incident to the Head of National Control, ESO.
The 1st communication between ENCC PSM and BEIS was at 17:41hrs.
The 1st communication with Ofgem was made just after 18:00hrs with the Director of Operations, ESO.
Further updates to BEIS from the PSM were made at 18:09hrs, 19:29hrs and 19:38hrs respectively.
Current ESO procedure outlines that following an event of loss of supply, a clear communication to Ofgem & BEIS is essential.
The communication is recommended to be initiated as soon as possible, and this procedure is in line with the ‘Energy Incident Reporting’ requirement set by Ofgem dated in December 2017.
It is important in all cases that resolution of the incident remains the primary objective.

segments.content: Part B heading
B1 ESO section 6.3 and Table 8 (timeline of external communications)
segments.transformation: Table 8 rows as printed (day heading, time, event, distribution); personal names replaced by the role in square brackets.

sources.section: 6.3 External Communications with Media and Wider Industry
sources.quote: The first ESO external communication was issued at 18:27hrs on 9 August.

sources.section: 6.3 External Communications with Media and Wider Industry
sources.quote: Table 8 provides the timeline of external communication with media and wider industry.

sources.section: 6.3 External Communications with Media and Wider Industry, Table 8 – Timeline of external communications (continues on PDF page 31)
sources.redaction: personal names replaced by the role in square brackets: Minister of State [name omitted]; [the Head of National Control]

sources.quote: Table 8 – Timeline of external communications

segments.content: B2 ESO section 6.4 (media statements by others)

sources.quote: In the ~90 minutes immediately following the initial fault on the network (starting at 17.09hrs) statements were issued by some DNOs and rail companies stating that the loss of power and subsequent disruption was the result of a National Grid fault.
These statements were issued ahead of any communication by the ESO and without engagement or coordination with the ESO communications team.
These public-facing communications did not impact the speed with which the incident was resolved but did drive a large volume of media queries to the ESO.

segments.content: B3 ESO appendices, Appendix M question 35

sources.quote: What issues did you encounter with the public-facing communications by industry, notably in terms of the content and timelines for the messaging?
The initial communications from some DNOs and rail companies said that the incident had been caused by a National Grid fault.
These communications were issued very shortly after the event (from 5.09pm onwards).
The ESO prepared an external communication seeking to give reassurance to the public which was issued at 18:27 once it was established that the DNOs had reconnected all customers.
The initial statements from some parts of the industry were issued before our statement and without any co-ordination with our comms team.

segments.content: B4 E3C interim report (communications, post-event announcement)

sources.quote: DNOs led local public communications during the event and the ESO did not publish public statements until after the disruption, meaning that energy partners (such as generators) were not directly informed.
In parallel with social media, DNOs reached out to customers via text message alert services and telephone services between 17:02 and 18:30.
Updates from the ESO followed the first set of restorations and were not publicly released until 18:27 via Twitter.

The Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy later announced via Twitter (10th August) and GOV.UK (14th August) that the government was to commission the Energy Emergencies Executive Committee to provide an interim and extended report into the power disruptions.

segments.content: B5 E3C final report section 5 (communication channels)

sources.quote: The first public announcement from ESO was issued at 18:27, which was following the event and once the system had stabilised.
By this time, many DNOs had used twitter to provide area updates that were widely circulated.
However, electricity generators received no communication during the events of 9 August that would have made them aware of the system condition.

segments.content: B6 Ofgem report paragraph 3.23 (Hornsea 1 communication with the ESO)

sources.quote: We have also found issues with Hornsea 1’s communication with the ESO.
Hornsea 1 did not notify the ESO directly when the wind farm deloaded by 737MW.
The wind farm then began its process of starting up two of its modules (temporarily) without
any coordination with the ESO whilst the ESO was attempting to respond to the generation losses it was aware of.

segments.content: Part C heading
C1 ESO section 6.4 call volumes and Table 9
segments.transformation: Table 9 cells as printed (thousands separators kept).

sources.quote: Electricity customers across GB can dial the ‘105’ customer helpline to get emergency help and advice, free of charge on mobile and landline phones.

Analysis of the volume of calls to the 105 helpline provides a useful indicator of the scale of customer impact across the DNOs and the timeframe for disruption to power supplies with calls dropping off dramatically post 6pm.

sources.section: 6.4 Call volumes to DNO's, Table 9 - Calls received by the 6 largest DNOs, during the period 4pm to 7pm on 9th August

sources.quote: Table 9 - Calls received by the 6 largest DNOs, during the period 4pm to 7pm on 9th August

segments.content: Part F heading
F1 Ofgem sets timeline for National Grid ESO report following UK power failures (press release, 12 August 2019)

sources.quote: Ofgem has written to the National Grid Electricity System Operator requesting an urgent interim report into the incident on 9 August 2019 to be provided to Ofgem by Friday 16 August.
A final, detailed technical report must be provided to Ofgem by Friday 6 September.

segments.content: F2 Business Secretary sets out scope of investigation into power cuts (press release, first published 2019-08-14T11:15:35+01:00)

sources.quote: National Grid has said power cuts had “nothing to do with changes in wind speed or the variability of wind”
The government today (14 August 2019) set out the scope of its review into the actions of the National Grid Electricity System Operator after Friday’s power cuts.
The committee met for the first time on Monday (12 August) and will provide a report on initial findings within 5 weeks to the Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy.
It will then submit a comprehensive report within 12 weeks.
This review will complement the investigation being undertaken by energy regulator Ofgem into how the electricity operator responded in line with its licence conditions and system security standards.

segments.content: F3 Great Britain power system disruption review (publication page; first published 2019-08-14T11:15:00+01:00, updated 2019-10-04 and 2020-01-03)

sources.quote: On Friday 9 August 2019 a power disruption resulted from the operation of Low Frequency Demand Disconnection relays on the Great Britain power system at about 4:54 pm.
Though demand was fully restored within 90 minutes, the secondary impacts continued to be felt for much of the day.

segments.content: F4 Ofgem launches investigation into power cuts (press release, 20 August 2019)

sources.quote: Ofgem has launched an investigation into the power cuts of Friday 9 August, following an initial report from National Grid Electricity System Operator (NGESO).

It will also seek to establish whether any of the parties involved – National Grid ESO, National Grid Electricity Transmission, 12* distribution network operators in England and Wales, as well as generators RWE Generation (Little Barford Power station) and Orsted (Hornsea) - breached their licence conditions.

Ofgem is liaising with the rail regulator (Office of Rail and Road) and will be engaging with the rail authorities to understand better why the drop in frequency on the energy network led to disruption for passengers.
The opening of this investigation does not imply that Ofgem has made any findings about non-compliance for any of the companies mentioned at this early stage of the investigation.

sources.quote: The file attached is a standard data extract from our Performance System Strategy (PSS) database
The information within the file contains all “attributed” delays to passenger train services in line with the guidance in the Delay Attribution Guide.

segments.content: A2 Publisher's explanation of the columns (quotations)

sources.quote: The data contains both delay and cancellation events (denoted by the performance event code) and a user should be careful when summing delay minutes (pfpi minutes) to exclude cancellation events.

It is possible that the detailed reasons for some of the delays in this file are still being investigated and until this is complete the responsibility for the delay is still not finalised (see attribution status).
Delay data is remapped to reflect the franchise mapping at the time of the data extraction (in this case May 2021).
trainids are unique within a railway period but not within a year
Train schedule type / traction type/ trailing load / unit class – these aren’t mandated or validated fields within PSS
Incident number – the TRUST DA incident number (not unique without the create date)
Incident create date – the date the incident was entered into the system
Incident start/end date – the date the system has the incident live (this is not the length of the incident on the ground)
Responsible Manager – who within the industry is responsible for the delay – all delays have responsibility for performance improvement purposes
Incident Reason – the Delay Attribution Guide cause code for the incident
Incident equipment – internal free form information
Incident description – short description of the incident for internal use
If no code the delay is primary (ie the delay is at the site of the incident) if reactionary the delay is a later consequence of that incident
A and M denote delays, C, D, O, P, S and F are cancellations … C – is a full cancelletion, D is a diversion, F is a failure to stop, S is a scheduled cancellation and O/P are part cancellations
Start/end stanox – the location of the delay (not the incident)
Event Datetime – the time the train encountered the delay

Pfpi minutes – the size of the delay …. Note if the train is cancelled (performance event code) a deemed delay minute is generated for internal usage in these circumstances the train hasn’t been delayed and including this delay in any calculation of delay is misleading.
Applicable timetable flag – if N the train is not in official performance records as it is a short term replacement of a train plan – normally a reinstatement of part of a cancelled service
